title: You want to lead… but God is watching how you serve.
paragraphs: You want to lead… but God is watching how you serve.

Stop.
Let that sink in.

You can build a platform…
and still be building it on pride.

You can speak with authority…
and still be empty in private.

You can be followed by thousands…
and still not be following Christ.
Here’s the uncomfortable truth most people avoid:

Some of us don’t want leadership…
we want recognition.

Not responsibility—
validation.

Not obedience—
attention.
And it’s subtle.
Dangerously subtle.
Because on the outside, it can still look “spiritual.”

You serve… but you need to be seen.
You give… but you hope it gets noticed.
You lead… but deep inside, you crave applause.
And when nobody claps?

Something inside you gets irritated.
Offended.
Restless.
That’s the exposure.
That’s where God puts His finger.
OPEN YOUR HEART HERE—this is where it gets real:
Why does silence feel like rejection?
Why does hidden service feel like loss?
Why does unseen obedience feel like it doesn’t count?
Because pride has been discipling us longer than Jesus has.

And pride doesn’t just shout—
it whispers.

“You deserve more.”
“You should be recognized.”
“They should notice you.”

And slowly…
your service becomes performance.
Your obedience becomes a strategy.
Your leadership becomes self-exaltation dressed in ministry language.

But then Jesus walks in—
and destroys the illusion.

“Whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant…
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”
Did you catch that?

Greatness = Servanthood.
Not influence.
Not visibility.
Not applause.
Servanthood.

And not the kind that gets posted.
The kind that gets ignored.

Jesus—
the King of Heaven—
washed feet that would walk away from Him.

He served people who misunderstood Him.
He loved people who would betray Him.
He gave His life for people who didn’t deserve Him.
That’s leadership.

Not climbing.
Descending.

Not being lifted up.
Laying yourself down.
📖 Philippians 2:5-8

“Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus…
He humbled Himself… becoming obedient to death—even death on a cross.”
This is where many stop.
Because this kind of leadership costs too much.

It will cost your ego.
Your need for validation.
Your desire to be noticed.
It will confront your hidden motives.
Expose your secret cravings.
Break your image.
And here’s the part we don’t say out loud:
Sometimes we serve God… while still trying to be God in our own story.

We want control.
Credit.
Recognition.
But the Cross crushes that.
Because the Gospel is not:
“Try harder to be humble.”
No.
The Gospel is this:

You are more sinful than you realize—
even your best acts can be mixed with pride.
📖 Isaiah 64:6
“All our righteous acts are like filthy rags…”
But you are also more loved than you can imagine.
Because Jesus didn’t wait for your motives to be pure.
He came anyway.
📖 Romans 5:8
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
That’s the turning point.
You don’t become a true leader by fixing your image.

You become a true leader
when you surrender your heart.

Sin → exposed
Pride → confronted
Heart → surrendered
Grace → received
Life → transformed

And only then…
you can finally serve without needing to be seen.
Because you’ve already been seen by God.
Fully.
Completely.
And still loved.
📖 Colossians 3:23-24

“Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord…
It is the Lord Christ you are serving.”
Read that again.

You are not serving people.
You are serving Christ.

Even when no one notices.
Even when no one thanks you.
Even when it feels invisible.
Nothing is wasted.
He sees it.

Every hidden act.
Every quiet sacrifice.
Every unseen obedience.

So let me ask you—
not to condemn you, but to call you higher:
If God removed the audience… would you still serve?
If no one clapped… would you still obey?
If nobody knew your name… would you still follow Jesus?
Because that’s where true leadership is born.
In secret.
In surrender.
In the quiet place where it’s just you and God.
This is your moment.
Not to perform.
Not to pretend.
But to return.
Lay down the need to be seen.
Lay down the hunger for applause.
Lay down the pride that’s been quietly driving your obedience.
And come back to Jesus.

Not as a performer—
but as a servant.

Not as someone impressive—
but as someone surrendered.
He’s not looking for perfect leaders.
He’s raising broken people who are willing to be remade by grace.
Pray this if you’re ready:

“Lord, expose every hidden pride in me.
Teach me to serve without needing to be seen.
Break my desire for applause.
Build in me a heart like Yours.
I surrender. In Jesus’ name.”
If this pierced your heart…
